# anndists

This crate provides distances computations used in some related crates [hnsw_rs](https://crates.io/crates/hnsw_rs), [annembed](https://crates.io/crates/annembed) and [coreset](https://github.com/jean-pierreBoth/coreset)

All distances implement the trait **Distance**:

```rust
pub trait Distance<T: Send + Sync> {  
    fn eval(&self, va: &[T], vb: &[T]) -> f32;
}
```

## Functionalities

The crate provides:

* usual distances as L1, L2, Cosine, Jaccard, Hamming for vectors of standard numeric types, Levenshtein distance on u16.

* Hellinger distance and Jeffreys divergence between probability distributions (f32 and f64). It must be noted that the Jeffreys divergence
(a symetrized Kullback-Leibler divergence) do not satisfy the triangle inequality. (Neither Cosine distance !).

* Jensen-Shannon distance between probability distributions (f32 and f64). It is defined as the **square root** of the Jensen-Shannon divergence and is a bounded metric. See [Nielsen F. in Entropy 2019, 21(5), 485](https://doi.org/10.3390/e21050485).

* A Trait to enable the user to implement its own distances.
  It takes as data slices of types T satisfying T:Serialize+Clone+Send+Sync. It is also possible to use C extern functions or closures.

* Simd implementation is provided for the most often used case.

## Implementation

Simd support is provided with the [simdeez](https://crates.io/crates/simdeez) crate on Intel and partial implementation with **std::simd** for general case.

## Building

### Simd

It is recommanded to use the compile flag **target-cpu=native** to activate dynamic cpu feature detection, for example
adding **RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native** in your environment.

* The simd provided by the simdeez crate is accessible with the feature "simdeez_f" for x86_64 or aarch64 processors.
Compile with **cargo build --release --features "simdeez_f"**.

* It is also possible to experiment with std::simd. Compiling with the feature stdsimd
(**cargo build --release --features "stdsimd"**), activates the  portable_simd feature on rust nightly. **This requires nightly compiler**.
Only the Hamming distance with the u32x16 and u64x8 types and DistL1,DistL2 and DistDot on f32*16 are provided for now.

## Benchmarks and Examples

The speed is illustated in the [hnsw_rs](https://crates.io/crates/hnsw_rs), [annembed](https://crates.io/crates/annembed) crates

# CRC32C

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/crc32c.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/crc32c)
[![Docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crc32c/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/crc32c/)
[![Travis](https://travis-ci.org/zowens/crc32c.svg?branch=master)](https://travis-ci.org/zowens/crc32c/)

Rust implementation of the CRC-32-Castagnoli algorithm with hardware acceleration where possible.

Hardware acceleration on the following architectures:
1. **x84-64** with [SSE 4.2](https://software.intel.com/sites/default/files/m/8/b/8/D9156103.pdf)
    * All stable versions of Rust
    * If SSE 4.2 is enabled at compile time, it will only build the SSE implementation. Otherwise, the `cpuid` is used to find the best implementation at runtime.
1. **aarch64** with [crc feature](https://developer.arm.com/documentation/dui0801/g/A32-and-T32-Instructions/CRC32C)
    * Only available on rust version >= 1.80.0 or nightly

All other processors utilize a software fallback.

## Usage

First, add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
crc32c = "0.6"
```

```rust
extern crate crc32c;

fn main() {
    let message = b"Hello world!";
    let crc = crc32c::crc32c(message);

    println!("hash = {}", crc);
}
```

# Paired measurement of the included 4B adapter

This experiment compares the pinned Qwen3.5-4B base model with the repository's
included `weights/coding-4b` adapter on 192 tool tasks and 64 arithmetic tasks.
It measures whether that adapter improves delivered answers on this panel.
It does not isolate the effect of MetaHarness, retrain the adapter, or authorize
model activation. The protocol is described in [ADR 016](../../docs/adr/ADR-016-paired-model-improvement-measurement.md).

**Current status: measured, keep.** The v3 freeze ran once on a rented Vast.ai
RTX 3090 through the [Vast host adapter](../../docs/adr/ADR-017-vast-host-adapter-and-live-paired-run.md)
($0.27). The local re-score of the retrieved raw responses matched the remote
report byte for byte, and the rental was confirmed destroyed. Tool tasks: base
123/192, adapter 173/192 (50 gains, 0 regressions, exact McNemar p = 1.8e-15).
Arithmetic: 63/64 in both arms. The preregistered rule is satisfied
(`research_improvement_confirmed: true`, no reasons). This is a research
qualification on a synthetic panel, not production activation.
Raw outputs, both reports, remote logs, receipts, the
[failure report](results/qwen35-4b-adapter-confirmation-v3/failure-report.json)
and a [dashboard](results/qwen35-4b-adapter-confirmation-v3/dashboard.html) are in
[results/qwen35-4b-adapter-confirmation-v3](results/qwen35-4b-adapter-confirmation-v3/).
Regenerate the breakdown with `tools/eval-report`, which refuses to write if its
counts disagree with `report.json`.

The committed [v3 protocol](frozen/v3/protocol.json) and
[256 cases](frozen/v3/cases.json) were frozen before generation. Protocol SHA256:
`bff9827e1ec8d77bc036519c562a1fb7240f820e64e9fb721c4ddeb2f772d3bc`. The cases are
byte-identical to v1 and v2. Those freezes are retired without output: v1's
shard-name check rejected the real model files, and v2 loaded the FP32 adapter
rounded to BF16 (see [STATUS.json](STATUS.json)). Do not alter a bundle after
generation.

## Freeze the panel before inference

Run from the repository root, with a new absolute output directory:

```bash
mkdir -p /workspace/measurement-runs
python3 experiments/model-improvement/prepare.py \
  --out /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-panel-v1
```

The bundle freezes the protocol, 256 cases and their expected answers. Do not
edit a frozen bundle or select tasks after inspecting model outputs. Use a new
run and disclose the change if the protocol needs revision. Tool prompts span
eight families with 24 cases each; arithmetic supplies a separate retained
capability anchor. Exact prompts are checked against the repository's existing
training, development, release and previous cross-model prompt sources. Shared
tool semantics remain: exact-text disjointness does not establish semantic
novelty, absence of pretraining contamination or general capability improvement.

## Prepare a GPU host

Use one CUDA-capable host for both arms, with sufficient memory to load the
entire 4B model in BF16. Freeze its environment before inference:

```bash
python3 -m pip install torch==2.11.0 transformers==5.12.1 \
  peft==0.21.2 safetensors==0.7.0
```

The worker checks these versions and CUDA availability. Choose a compatible
CUDA/PyTorch distribution on the host rather than changing the protocol to
accept an unmeasured environment. Host package installation and weight download
are preparation steps, outside the inference worker. For example, download the
public pinned snapshot using the host's approved network path:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
assets = json.loads(Path("experiments/model-improvement/model-assets.json").read_text())
snapshot_download(
    repo_id="Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B",
    revision="851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a",
    local_dir="/workspace/models/Qwen3.5-4B-851bf6e",
    token=False,
    allow_patterns=[*assets["asset_files"], "model*.safetensors"],
)
PY
```

Transfer the frozen bundle, the repository source and `weights/coding-4b` to
the host. Keep provider credentials at the authenticated host; bundles and
measurement artifacts contain no secret references that need resolution by
model code. The worker uses local files, disables remote model code and checks
model shard and adapter hashes before inference.

## Run both arms and score their saved outputs

After preparing the GPU host, the paired run also has a single host command:

```bash
python3 experiments/model-improvement/run-pair.py \
  --bundle /workspace/ruvllm/experiments/model-improvement/frozen/v3 \
  --model-dir /workspace/models/Qwen3.5-4B-851bf6e \
  --adapter-dir /workspace/ruvllm/weights/coding-4b \
  --out /workspace/measurement-runs/paired-v3 --deadline-seconds 5400
```

It launches fresh sequential processes for both arms, stops on failure, and runs
the scorer only after both arms succeed. It provisions no GPU or credentials.
The GPU loop's trusted host adapter can invoke this command on its allocated
worker. The host must inspect the actual report and executor response before
acknowledging completion; completing a measurement is separate from finding a
positive improvement.

Use distinct, nonexistent absolute output directories. Run the arms sequentially
on the same idle host with unchanged software, device and generation settings:

```bash
python3 experiments/model-improvement/worker.py \
  --bundle /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-panel-v1 \
  --model-dir /workspace/models/Qwen3.5-4B-851bf6e \
  --adapter-dir /workspace/ruvllm/weights/coding-4b \
  --out /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-base-v1 \
  --arm base --deadline-seconds 1800

python3 experiments/model-improvement/worker.py \
  --bundle /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-panel-v1 \
  --model-dir /workspace/models/Qwen3.5-4B-851bf6e \
  --adapter-dir /workspace/ruvllm/weights/coding-4b \
  --out /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-adapter-v1 \
  --arm adapter --deadline-seconds 1800

python3 experiments/model-improvement/measurement.py \
  --bundle /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-panel-v1 \
  --base-run /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-base-v1 \
  --adapter-run /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-adapter-v1 \
  --out /workspace/measurement-runs/qwen35-4b-report-v1
```

Both arms load the same BF16 backbone with the same `PeftModel` wrapper and
verify the same 32 adapter tensors at their trained precision.
The base arm uses `disable_adapter()`; the adapter arm enables the adapter.
Greedy decoding, disabled thinking, seed 20261103 and a 512-new-token limit are
identical. An incomplete deadline-limited run cannot produce a qualifying
report. Run a new pair if it must be repeated; never combine selected outputs
from different runs.

Each arm saves `runtime.json`, `responses.jsonl` and a completion record emitted
only after all cases finish. The scorer validates identities, hashes, coverage,
runtime bindings and complete output before writing `report.json`. Preserve
the bundle, full raw responses, both runtime/completion records and the report
together. The report is the source for numerical claims; stdout from a model
or a provider status message is not evidence of improvement.

The primary result is delivered exact tool-call accuracy over 192 paired cases.
Only the expected call and exact typed arguments pass. The 64 arithmetic cases
require the expected boxed integer. Missing, malformed, truncated or incorrect
answers count as incorrect. Model-produced programs and tool calls are scored
as data and are never executed. The report includes paired wins/losses, exact
two-sided McNemar p-values and retained-capability/completion checks.

Research qualification requires a positive tool accuracy difference, primary
McNemar p < 0.05, no arithmetic accuracy regression and no completion decrease.
A positive point estimate alone is insufficient. The small, templated panel and
single checkpoint/seed do not support broad model-quality or production claims.
Latency is descriptive: one sequential pair does not establish a speedup.

## Use with the scheduled GPU loop

The existing [GPU loop](../../integrations/metaharness/GPU-LOOP.md) can hand work
to an operator-configured, pinned host adapter. This experiment does not add a
ruOS or Vast.ai API and does not turn the filesystem spool into a GPU executor.
The trusted host must prepare local files, run both worker arms, invoke the
scorer and retain verified artifacts before deriving a successful structured
completion for the scheduler. An `experiment.configPath`/`planPath` in an
existing loop configuration retains its existing native-experiment semantics;
it is not a new worker command interface.

Keep ruOS secret resolution, provider spending enforcement and allocation
cleanup at that host, under the existing job/run/idempotency bindings. Do not
convert agent-written JSON or mere process submission into verified completion.
No paid job, recurring schedule or provider allocation is enabled by these
commands or the local contract tests. Qualification of this research panel
does not bypass the existing external activation gates.

## Build the regression dashboard

After retrieving the complete pair, rerun the frozen scorer and group each
base pass that became an adapter failure by expected tool and observed failure.
The dashboard keeps case IDs for lookup in the raw outputs. It does not render
model output or alter the qualification rule.

```sh

  --bundle experiments/model-improvement/frozen/v1 \
  --base /workspace/measurement-runs/paired-v1/base \
  --adapter /workspace/measurement-runs/paired-v1/adapter \
```

# Frozen Vast cloud comparison

This experiment compares five BF16 artifacts from three models across two Qwen families. It measures two distinct interventions: the published Qwen3.5 0.8B sparse repair and the previously selected Qwen3.5 4B coding adapter. Qwen3 Coder 30B A3B is an unchanged coding reference. No edit is transferred between architectures. No result authorizes deployment or establishes state of the art.

The prior local 16 problem repair experiment failed its quality gate. This cloud experiment tests broader behavior with stronger output budgets and records failures as well as successes.

| Panel | Cases per direct arm | Maximum output tokens per case |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| HumanEval, original tests with frozen complete function chat prompts | 164 | 2048 |
| Existing synthetic coding tool release fixtures | 27 | 2048 |
| Original procedural integer arithmetic | 128 | 8192 |

Five direct arms and two additional 0.8B thinking math arms completed 1,851 generations and 2,552,202 output tokens. The [completed report](results/cross-model-20261103/README.md) explains the measurements and regressions. The frozen cap was 9,295,872 output tokens. Its original planning assumption of 500 aggregate tokens per second implied 5.2 hours for the cap alone; that assumption is not a measured speed. The worker retained its original absolute deadline. Downloads, model loading, package installation and native compilation consumed lease time. The rental and temporary guard resources were removed and independently read back as absent.

## Pins and scope

The three [official model cards](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B), [4B model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B), and [Coder model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct) declare Apache 2.0 licensing. `models.json` records immutable revisions and published Safetensors SHA256 values. The original [HumanEval source](https://github.com/openai/human-eval/tree/b9453e8f1865df0a0057a1383767caa400acfbcf) is MIT licensed; this chat evaluation is not its official leaderboard protocol. Pretraining contamination is unknown.

Runtime is vLLM 0.21.0, Transformers 5.12.1 and Torch 2.11.0, using the pinned amd64 container in `protocol.json`. The [vLLM 0.21 registry](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.21.0/vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py) supports the relevant Qwen architectures. Its [Docker source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.21.0/docker/Dockerfile) uses CUDA 13.0.2. Runtime versions, all installed packages, GPU identity, driver, model tree digests, frozen prompt digests, token IDs, termination reason, and batch timing are recorded. Temperature is zero, the seed and batch order are fixed, prefix caching is disabled, and every arm starts in a new process. Hardware dependent numeric differences remain possible.

The FP32 LoRA matrices merge as `BF16(FP32(W) + 2 B A)` into the 16 authorized 4B down projection tensors. Every untouched tensor is compared to its original bytes, and the base checkpoint remains unchanged. This measures BF16 deployment of the selected adapter, separately from earlier MLX 4 bit measurements.

Both official Coder EOS IDs, 151645 and 151643, are explicit stops. Qwen3.5 uses tokenizer chat end token 248046 and model configuration end of text token 248044. The unused initial freeze was archived before any GPU generation when the secondary Coder stop was identified. Corpus and budgets did not change.

The first cloud runtime attempt is preserved under `archive/unused-runtime-attempt-01`. Its unscored preflight stopped before LLM construction because the declared stop set omitted the tokenizer chat end token 248046. Inspection also confirmed that Transformers 5.12.1 defaults to a dictionary from `apply_chat_template`. Before any model generation, the Qwen3.5 stop sets were corrected to include both declared end tokens, and the worker explicitly requested a flat token ID list with `return_dict=False`. Original source files, freezes, runtime signature, EOS configuration evidence, and the exact failure log are archived. The intermediate tokenizer only fix was never uploaded or run and is separately archived. All other experimental settings and fixtures are unchanged.

## Public reproduction scope

The historical scorer is preserved exactly at [frozen/ruflo_model/scoring.py](frozen/ruflo_model/scoring.py). The unchanged protocol still records its original relative location and digest; [the explicit source map](frozen/source-map.json) records this single relocation. `scripts/check_repository.py` verifies all eight frozen implementation files and frozen inputs. The current root scorer separately fixes macOS framework Python launcher compatibility. Historical source verification does not execute that corrected scorer, and these saved results were not regenerated with it. A future experiment using the corrected scorer needs a new freeze.

This source directory preserves the frozen research implementation, case corpus, protocol, model revisions, licenses, correction history and [completed results](results/cross-model-20261103/README.md). The separate [evidence release](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruvllm/releases/tag/cloud-evidence-20261103) contains all 1,851 responses, the original native source archive, historical native executable and preparation wrapper. The source checkout omits those larger historical artifacts. Provider credentials, account configuration, private lifecycle receipts and the complete worker filesystem are excluded from public distribution. def integer_expression(expression):
    operations = {ast.Add: operator.add, ast.Sub: operator.sub, ast.Mult: operator.mul}

    def visit(node):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and type(node.value) is int:
            return node.value
        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp) and type(node.op) in operations:
            return operations[type(node.op)](visit(node.left), visit(node.right))
        raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected arithmetic syntax: {ast.dump(node)}")

    return visit(ast.parse(expression, mode="eval").body)

            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid batch duration"):
